releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.129
releases.body:
## Bug fixes

- **Draft-assisted replies no longer pile up memory, and run faster on long conversations.** While a draft-assisted (DFlash) model wrote a reply to a large conversation, the memory the Mac must keep in RAM could jump by several gigabytes mid-reply. Working buffers left over from each draft round are now handed back once they pass 2 GB. On the 35B draft-assisted model with a 34,000-token conversation, that memory peaked at 2 GB instead of 7.6 GB, and replies rose from 49.8 to about 60 tokens per second.
- **Status updates during draft-assisted replies.** The memory figures on the status page now change while a draft-assisted model writes, instead of staying fixed for the whole reply.

## Compatibility

- No setting, command or local API changed. Replies from plain models are unchanged.
- Conversations, downloaded models, the prompt store on disk and every setting are kept.
- Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.

## Distribution

The app and disk image are signed with the project's Developer ID, notarized and stapled by Apple, and the update is signed with the project's Sparkle key.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.128
releases.body:
## Bug fixes

- **A long reply no longer slows down the rest of the Mac.** While a model wrote a long reply to a large conversation, video could freeze, audio could glitch and windows could respond slowly, and it got worse the longer the reply ran. Each time the conversation's attention buffers grew, the outgrown copies were kept instead of being handed back, so the memory the Mac must keep in RAM climbed until it reached the system's ceiling. They are now handed back as the reply is written. With a 34,000-token conversation and a 3,500-token reply on a 35B model, that memory ended at 30.3 GB instead of 39.2 GB and stayed flat throughout, at the same reply speed.

## Known

- Replies from a draft-assisted (DFlash) model can still show a one-step memory rise after a freshly read large prompt. This is tracked and not fixed in this release.

## Compatibility

- No setting, command or local API changed.
- Conversations, downloaded models and every setting are kept.
- macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.

## Distribution

The app and disk image are signed with the project's Developer ID, built with the Hardened Runtime, and notarized and stapled by Apple. Existing installations receive this release through the in-app update.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.127
releases.body:
## Count this Mac once a day, if you agree

From the second day you use Astronomical, the chat window asks once, "May this Mac be counted?", and shows the exact line this Mac would send, such as `Astronomical 0.2.127 · macOS 27.2 · Apple M5 Pro · 48 GB`.

- **Nothing is sent unless you choose "Count this Mac".** "No thanks" is final.
- **One line a day,** with the app version, macOS version, chip and memory, and no identifier, so one day's line cannot be linked to another's.
- **Turn it on or off** under "What leaves this Mac" in Settings, which also shows when it last went.

## Clearer failures

A model whose files are damaged now says so in plain words, "This model's files are damaged or incomplete. Remove the model and download it again.", instead of "The engine stopped answering".

## Fixes

- "Send reports like this without asking" and the problem report choice in Settings now save from the chat window.
- Only the chat window, Observatory and tools can change sharing choices or send a report; other pages on this Mac are refused.

## Compatibility

- Existing settings load unchanged.
- Conversations, downloaded models and every setting are kept.
- macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.

Signed with the project's Developer ID, notarized and stapled by Apple.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.126
releases.body:
## Tell the developers when something breaks, if you choose to

When a model will not load, a reply runs out of graphics memory or stops on a fatal error, a catalog download fails its checks, or the engine stops unexpectedly, the chat window now offers a short problem report under the failure message.

- **You see the whole report first.** Nothing is sent unless you press Send report. You can add a note in your own words, or choose to send such reports without being asked.
- **What a report holds:** the app version; your Mac's chip, memory and macOS version; the catalog model in use, or only "a model not in the catalog"; the kind of problem with the step that failed; how the engine stopped, if it did; and the engine's last few events as fixed phrases with numbers. Never your prompts, conversations, files, images, folder names or log lines.
- **Where it goes:** to the project's error-reporting receiver, which does not store internet addresses or work out a location.

## What leaves this Mac

Settings has a new list of everything Astronomical can send and when, your choice for problem reports (ask each time, always send, never), every report already sent as the exact lines that went, and "Report a problem" for things no error catches, such as slow replies. Nothing is asked at first launch, and no usage counts are collected. The privacy page describes all of this.

## Compatibility

- Existing settings load unchanged; the new `sharing` section is optional.
- Conversations, downloaded models and every setting are kept.
- macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.

Signed with the project's Developer ID, notarized and stapled by Apple.

releases.name: Astronomical 0.2.125
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Give a model's memory back on request.** A loaded model holds many gigabytes of memory until Astronomical unloads it after a quiet spell. Programs and agents can now ask for that memory back at once with `POST /v1/control/unload-model` on the local API. The next request loads the model again. A reply that is being written is never interrupted: the request answers "busy" instead.
- **The Astronomical skill tells agents about it,** so an agent that has finished its job can free the memory when you ask.

## Compatibility

- Your settings, conversations and downloaded models are kept. No setting changed.
- Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.

The app and disk image are signed with Developer ID, notarized and stapled by Apple, and the update feed is signed.
